D: An American soldier goes absent without leave to fight in a secret, brutal martial arts tournament in Hong Kong.
P: Serve the snacks when Ray and Frank arrive in Hong Kong.
S: Batter of flour, eggs, sugar, evaporated milk and a little custard powder, cooked in an egg waffle pan until crisp outside, soft inside.
a Hong Kong street stall classic
Fish balls simmered in a curry sauce of curry powder, garlic, coconut milk and a little sugar, served on skewers.
Frank and Ray playing the arcade game in Hong Kong

Fluffy steamed buns filled with diced char siu pork in a sticky oyster, hoisin and sugar sauce, steamed until puffed and split open on top. Dice 300g char siu pork. Fry a diced shallot, add 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp hoisin, 1 tbsp sugar and 100ml water, thicken with 1 tsp cornflour and stir in the pork. Cool. Mix 300g bao flour, 5g dried yeast, 30g sugar and 160ml warm water into a soft dough, knead 8 minutes and prove 1 hour. Divide into 12, fill, pinch closed and prove 20 minutes. Steam 12 minutes.
M: Pork and prawn wontons in a clear chicken, ginger and dried shrimp broth with thin egg noodles, blanched choy sum and a drizzle of sesame oil. Simmer 1.5L chicken stock with 4 slices ginger and 1 tbsp dried shrimp for 20 minutes, then season with soy and white pepper. Mix 200g pork mince, 200g chopped green prawns, sesame oil and soy, and fold into 24 wonton wrappers. Boil the wontons for 3 minutes. Cook 300g thin egg noodles for 1 minute and blanch 2 bunches choy sum. Divide into bowls, top with wontons and pour over the hot broth.
the night before the final fight
Rump steak strips marinated in soy and cornflour, stir-fried hard with onion, capsicum and garlic, finished with lots of cracked black pepper and oyster sauce, over steamed rice.
W: Puff pastry pressed into tart tins, filled with a custard of eggs, milk, evaporated milk and sugar strained until silky, baked at 200C for 15 minutes until just set and wobbly.
K: the cha chaan teng café round the corner
Strong black tea simmered 5 minutes, strained through a fine cloth, mixed with evaporated milk and sugar, served hot or over ice.

s.how: Whisk 150g flour, 2 tbsp custard powder, 2 tsp baking powder and 80g sugar. Add 2 eggs and 200ml evaporated milk plus 100ml water and whisk smooth. Rest 30 minutes. Cook in a hot greased egg waffle pan for 3 minutes a side until crisp and golden.

s.note: a Hong Kong street stall classic
s.how: Fry 2 tbsp curry powder and crushed garlic in oil for a minute. Add 400ml coconut milk, a spoon of sugar and a little water and simmer 5 minutes. Add 500g fish balls and simmer for 10 minutes until hot through. Thread onto skewers and spoon over the sauce.

m.note: the night before the final fight
m.how: Slice 600g rump steak thinly and marinate in soy and a spoon of cornflour for 20 minutes. Stir-fry hard in a very hot wok, then add sliced onion, green capsicum and garlic. Finish with oyster sauce and a big spoon of cracked black pepper. Serve over jasmine rice.

w.how: Cut puff pastry into rounds and press into a patty tin. Whisk 3 eggs with 150ml milk, 100ml evaporated milk and 80g sugar until dissolved, then strain until silky. Fill the cases and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until just set and still wobbly in the centre.

d.note: the cha chaan teng café round the corner
d.how: Simmer 6 black tea bags in 750ml water for 5 minutes until very strong. Strain through a fine cloth or sieve into a jug. Stir in evaporated milk and sugar to taste. Serve hot in cups, or chill and pour over ice in tall glasses.
